subject: EdgeAir: data provenance, keystore & operator isolation questionnaire

Subject: EdgeAir questionnaire: provenance, keystore, and operator isolation

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As part of our procurement review we've pulled together a short focused questionnaire around artifact provenance, keystore management, and operator isolation for offline/air-gapped deployments. The attached overview (EdgeAir_RFP_Qs.pdf) lists the items we need by Tuesday EOD:

- Description of key storage options for Private deployments (on-prem HSM, cloud-provisioned HSM, software-keystore fallback)
- Key rotation and compromise recovery procedures
- How model and container artifacts are signed and verified before installation (supply-chain attestations, SBOMs, signature verification tooling)
- Network and operator isolation controls for air-gapped sites (allowed maintenance paths, signed bundle process)
- Evidence of cryptographic attestation (any third-party attestation or internal attestations you can share)

Can you confirm whether you can provide an initial response and artifacts by 2026-09-11? If helpful, we can split into technical and compliance deliverables.

Best,
Devon Hayes

Devon —

Thanks, we've started compiling answers. I've attached a working spreadsheet that maps your questions to our product features and the artifacts we'll provide (EA_Q_v2.xlsx). High-level notes inline below; Rafael and Naomi are looped in for detail and attachments.

Summary (high level):
- Keystore options: Redwood Private supports customer-managed HSMs (FIPS 140-2/3 certified HSMs such as Thales/Cavium or cloud HSM integrations), a catalog of approved external KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), and an encrypted software keystore for lab/staging only (not for regulated installs). We provide an HSM-backed mode for on-prem installs and an HSM-binding guide for VPC deployments.

- Rotation & recovery: We offer automated rotation policies configurable per-tenant (recommended 90-day rotation) with documented emergency key compromise procedures including key revocation, re-signing artifacts, and rollback to known-good snapshots.

- Artifact provenance: Build-time signing via reproducible pipelines (cosign/notary v2 recommended). We publish SBOMs and SLSA-style build attestations for verified model artifacts and runtime constituents. Rafael will attach a sample keystore attestation and a short writeup on our signing pipeline.

- Air-gapped maintenance: For sealed sites we support "signed-bundle" updates: offline-signed bundles verified by local install-time verifier. Operator roles are separated; maintenance bundles are validated with a chain of signatures and require quorum approval by named operators. Naomi will share an operator checklist and runbook excerpt.

We will provide: km-keystore-attestation.pdf (sample attestation), operator-checklist.txt, and a network-diagram.png showing allowed egress paths for emergency updates. Rafael/Naomi — can you review the spreadsheet and add the technical artifacts we promised? Devon — confirm whether you need third-party attestation or internal artifacts for procurement.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Engineering

Subject: Re: EdgeAir questionnaire: provenance, keystore, and operator isolation

Kimberly / Devon —

Attaching the focused security write-up and a sample HSM attestation: km-keystore-attestation.pdf. Key points (short):

1) HSM / keystore modes
- On-prem HSM: Redwood supports PKCS#11-compatible HSMs (FIPS 140-2/3). Customers can provide a Thales/HSM appliance; our installer binds keys via a keystore agent which enforces non-exportable keys.
- Cloud KMS: For VPC deployments we integrate with customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) using mutual TLS and role-bound service identities.
- Software fallback: Encrypted keystore using AES-GCM with a passphrase-protected keywrap; explicitly documented as non-production for regulated workloads.

2) Rotation and compromise recovery
- Rotation: Recommended 90-day rotation; automatic rotation API for workload keys. For root signing keys we recommend manual rotation with multi-operator signing during key rollover.
- Compromise recovery: Procedure: revoke key -> publish new signing key -> re-sign latest artifacts -> roll-forward deployment with validated signature chain. We keep a cryptographically-signed chain-of-trust for models (timestamped signatures) so older versions can be verified post-incident.

3) Artifact signing & provenance
- Pipeline: We support reproducible build artifacts with SLSA v1/v2 attestations and cosign signatures. Runtime verifies signatures at install time against a locally pinned root trust bundle.
- SBOMs: Generated at build time ( SPDX + CycloneDX ) and included in the signed bundle. We can produce a redacted SBOM for procurement reviews.
- Notary / transparency: We can publish artifact digests to a transparency log (optionally third-party) and provide proof-of-origin for installed models.

4) Air-gap maintenance path (operational details)
- Signed bundle: Update bundles are produced in CI, signed by pipeline keys, then signed by at least two named operators (quorum), and delivered via physical media or a temporary, strictly-scoped jump-host session.
- Verifier: Local installer includes a verified verification binary that checks signature chain, SBOM presence, and timestamp before applying changes.
- Emergency egress: All outbound operation requires operator-initiated ephemeral connection via an auditable bastion; no persistent outbound sockets are allowed.

Attached: km-keystore-attestation.pdf (sample cert), a CLI snippet showing cosign verification, and a short JSON example of our SBOM manifest (redacted in attachment). Let us know if EdgeAir needs a notarized third-party attestation; we have partnerships for independent FIPS/HSM audits.

- Rafael
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Devon/Kim —

Quick ops checklist attached (operator-checklist.txt) and a short runbook excerpt below for sealed-site maintenance. This reflects our current practice for on-prem sealed installs and the minimal human steps required:

- Pre-step: Prepare signed bundle in CI; include SBOM + cosign signatures + timestamp and at least two operator signatures.
- Transport: Deliver bundle on encrypted media or coordinate a one-time jump-host session initiated from the site through a named bastion IP (we provide ephemeral VPN creds).
- Local validation: Run local verifier (sha256 digest check, signature chain validation against local root bundle, SBOM presence).
- Install: Operator invokes the installer; installer writes a signed installation receipt to local audit store (immutable append-only log) and returns the operation digest to the central audit endpoint when connectivity is available.
- Rollback: Installer can roll back to prior signed snapshot; rollback requires operator approval recorded in audit store.

Operator separation: we enforce RBAC for operator accounts and require multi-person approval for root key operations. There are documented operator on-call flows for emergency use of jump-hosts.

I'll add the runbook excerpt and the operator checklist to the shared Drive link: https://redwood.example.com/drive/EA-evidence. Rafael — can you include the cosign example as a small script in that folder?

Thanks,
